bug_report: Stacked discounts compute the wrong total. Two 50% discounts on $100 give $0 instead of $25 - they're applied to the original amount in parallel instead of compounding. Fix apply_discounts so stacked discounts combine correctly. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py.

conversations.text: Our discount stacking is wrong - two 50%-off coupons on a $100 item zero it out instead of leaving $25. And finance says even when it's not zero, mixed coupons don't match their model.
apply_discounts sums the percentages and applies once, so 50% + 50% = 100% off. I'll make them compound sequentially, applying each to the running amount - that gives $25 for the two-50%-off case.
That's only half of it. With a percent coupon plus a fixed-dollar coupon, the result depends on which order they were entered, and customers were ordering them to their advantage.
So the order needs to be fixed rather than submission order. Should the fixed-dollar amount come off first, or the percentage?
Percent first, always. Then the fixed amount.

Got it - apply all percent discounts first (compounding), then fixed-amount ones, ignoring submission order. So $10-off + 50%-off on $100 is 50 then minus 10 = $40 either way. Deterministic: percent before fixed.
